slides.text:
Claude Code. Cursor. Copilot. Windsurf. Aider. Cline.

I've used them all. Some for months. Some I dropped in <accent>days</accent>.

Here's an honest breakdown of what actually works and which one I <accent>ship code</accent> with.

slides.heading: 204 Tools. <accent>One Landscape.</accent>
slides.caption: ToolShelf tracks 204 AI coding tools in 2026. The terminal is the new IDE.

slides.heading: The Old Way vs <accent>Agentic</accent> Coding
before: Tab-complete one line at a time

slides.heading: Claude <accent>Code</accent>
slides.body:
- 46% developer satisfaction (highest)
- Terminal-native agentic coding
- Skills, Hooks, MCP integrations
- 5.5x more token-efficient than Cursor
- $20/mo Pro | $100/mo Max

terminal.text: > Fix the auth bug in login.ts
Found issue: token expiry not checked
All 12 tests passing. Ready to commit.

slides.heading: <accent>Cursor</accent> IDE
slides.body:
- 19% satisfaction, AI-first VS Code fork
- Composer + Agent + Background agents
- Visual Editor for drag-and-drop UI
- Credit-based billing (watch burn rate)
- $20/mo Pro | $40/mo Business

terminal.text: > Add dark mode to the settings page

slides.heading: Claude Code vs Cursor: <accent>Clear Winner?</accent>
slides.caption: Builder.io's deep dive comparison. Claude Code uses 5.5x fewer tokens for identical tasks.

slides.heading: GitHub <accent>Copilot</accent>
slides.body:
- 42% market share, 20M+ users
- Multi-model: Claude, GPT, Gemini
- Coding Agent auto-solves GitHub issues
- Deepest GitHub integration
- $10/mo Pro | $39/mo Pro+

slides.heading: The <accent>Stats</accent> Don't Lie
slides.caption: 85% of devs use AI coding tools. Copilot leads market share. But satisfaction tells a different story.

slides.heading: The <accent>Other</accent> 3 Worth Knowing
items: Windsurf ($15/mo) - Cheapest AI IDE, ranked #1 by LogRocket, acquired by Cognition AI
Aider (Free + API) - Open source, works with ANY model, best Git integration
Cline (Free + API) - VS Code extension, plan-then-act mode, MCP support, 5M+ devs

slides.heading: Terminal vs <accent>IDE</accent> Tools
before: Claude Code: Full autonomy, best context
Cline: VS Code, transparent, open source

slides.heading: Pick Your <accent>Tool</accent>
items: Free + open source? Aider or Cline

slides.text:
I use Claude Code to ship.
Cursor when I need to see the code.
Copilot for autocomplete.

The best setup isn't one tool.
It's knowing when to use which.

slides.heading: My <accent>Stack</accent> in 2026
slides.body:
Primary: Claude Code (90% of my work)
Secondary: Cursor for visual editing
Autocomplete: Copilot for quick completions

Claude Code changed how I build.
I think in outcomes, not lines of code.
